Element Energy (2021). Net-Zero Industrial Pathways (N-ZIP) Model: User Guide and Assumptions Log (model version 1.1). Prepared for the Climate Change Committee and the Department for Business, Energy and Industrial Strategy (BEIS), March 2021. R. Simon, J. Martins, E. Durusut, A. Mitchell, A. Mattos, F. Tahir, M. Joos, S. Lyons. Cambridge: Element Energy Ltd.

A 96-slide user guide and assumptions log for the N-ZIP Excel model (companion to element-energy_2020_001). Like the report, it does NOT print the technology data tables: FSNewBuildCosts, FSRetrofitCost, ProcessCounterfactualsNew, CaptureTechnologyFuelConsumption and FFPFECost are described (names, sources, method) but their values live only in the N-ZIP workbook; counterfactual and fuel-switch costs are said to come mostly from the BEIS 2018 Industrial Fuel Switching Market Engagement Study (element-energy_2018_001, held), with hydrogen sizing exponents from Hy4Heat WP6. So the to-get need (tabulated capex/opex/efficiency by sector and equipment) is NOT met; the N-ZIP model workbook itself would be needed. Loaded (main file, 4 technologies): capture-rate 95% and 25-yr lifetime for first-generation amines, advanced amines or blends and calcium looping; availability windows; HIsarna+CCS derived capex (212 USD/(t/y) x 1.5, includes capture), lifetime, 20% emission reduction. Loaded to _other-values: the p.42 CINDY capture-technology table for 8 technologies (capex in GBP million with no reference plant size printed, opex as fraction of capex, inlet/outlet CO2 concentration and pressure), sizing exponent, FOAK/SOAK/NOAK factors, higher-capture-rate cost factor, boiler efficiency for capture heat (90%), network upgrade cost, optimism bias, cost of capital, flue-gas CO2 concentrations by process, ATR capture rate, HHV/LHV table, carbon values. Not loaded: other scenario parameters, T&S first-year tables, transport selection charts (no numbers), output column lists. Locator: printed slide numbers, equal to PDF pages. The model works on an LHV basis (p.40, p.68). Trap: p.45 says CINDY 2013 GBP capex were converted to 2019 GBP "resulting in 110% increase", and does not say whether the p.42 table shows 2013 or 2019 values.
